title: Structural Masquerading via Pointer Casts (STRUCT_CAST_MASQUERADE)
pattern: Casting a pointer/reference of one struct to another struct under the assumption that they share a layout prefix (structural inheritance masquerade).
why_bad: It bypasses compiled abstraction boundaries and relies entirely on layout prefix stability. Under compiler optimizations (and Rust's default layout non-determinism), field ordering is not guaranteed to match. Rearranging fields in either struct results in silent, catastrophic memory corruption.
detection: Look for unsafe raw pointer casts (`as *const ... as *const ...`) converting a larger struct reference to a prefix-compatible smaller struct.
fix: Extract shared structural data into a nested field (composition) or define a shared Trait representing coordinate accessors.
source: *Robert C. Martin - Clean Architecture (2017)*, Chapter 5 (Inheritance); *Martin Fowler - Refactoring, 1st Edition (1999)*, page 239.
